item.title: Women researchers complete Lae training
item.description: Twelve women researchers have completed a four-day training in Lae to strengthen their research skills and improve the quality of their work. The training ended on Thursday, October 8, at Lae International Hotel under the Australian Government-supported Strongim Risets Kapasiti Bilong Ol Meri (SRKBOM) program.
item.content:encoded:
Twelve women researchers have completed a four-day training in Lae to strengthen their research skills and improve the quality of their work.

The training ended on Thursday, October 8, at Lae International Hotel under the Australian Government-supported Strongim Risets Kapasiti Bilong Ol Meri (SRKBOM) program.

The workshop covered data analysis, research methods, interviewing and reviewing existing studies.

Australian Consul-General Brenton Kanowski said women researchers played an important role in producing evidence to guide decisions and shape policies.

“When women help frame the questions, lead the inquiry and present the evidence, decision-making becomes stronger and more representative,” Mr Kanowski said.

He said Australia was proud to support women’s leadership and research capacity in Papua New Guinea.

Earlier this year, the 12 researchers spent a month in Brisbane and Melbourne to gain experience in the Australian academic environment.

The program also has groups in Port Moresby and Goroka.

A women’s research alumni network was scheduled to launch in Port Moresby on October 9 to help participants maintain professional connections and share knowledge.

item.content:encoded:
‎At least ten international Cocoa and chocolate experts are in the country visiting local cocoa farmers, this week, in the Amazon Bay in Central Province, accompanied by PNGs own Queen Emma Chocolate of Paradise Food industry General Manager, Karina Makori. ‎ ‎The team arrived in Alotau, Milne Bay Province, over the weekend before travelling by road and motorboat to Amazon Bay. ‎ ‎This is the second cocoa tourism adventure by international experts to PNG, aimed at giving the cocoa tourist first-hand experience about rural cocoa farming.

Led by New Zealand's Cacao Ambassador, Oonagh Brown of Weave Cacao, together with PNGs very own Queen Emma Chocolate of Paradise Food industry General Manager Karina Makori, the visit to Amazon Bay is to give these visitors the opportunity to experience and understand what it truly takes to be a rural cocoa farmer. ‎ ‎"I always endeavored to go remote to communities that have never been visited before. Bringing these chocolate makers so they can actually see the trees, meet the farmers and really understand what it takes for cocoa to be available for them overseas. ‎ ‎"This way we can create a bridge between world market and the actual farmers," Ms. Brown said. ‎ ‎Ms. Brown says the cocoa tour also includes young people who have been engaged in Cocoa farming overseas, and they will share their experiences with the local youths to help them understand the income potential on cocoa farming. ‎ ‎"There's a disconnect with youths being cocoa farmers, so this is inspiring to show them that there's a whole new way possible through cocoa," she said. ‎ ‎The team is currently in Amazon Bay and expected to return to Alotau, Milne Bay Province, at the end of the week to visit other local cocoa farmers. ‎ ‎Brown led PNGs first cocoa tourism tour in November 2025, to Makamaka LLG in Alotau District, Milne Bay Province, and this year, she's led another group of cocoa and chocolate experts to Amazon Bay in Central Province to experience and learn, as recipients, where their cocoa and chocolate is being farmed.

item.title: SP joins Chiefs as major partner
item.description: Papua New Guinea Chiefs have welcomed SP Lager on board as the latest Major Partner with the new franchise preparing to make their debut in the 2028 NRL Season. The three-year partnership further strengthens the brand’s long-standing connection to rugby league and communities across the country.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea Chiefs have welcomed SP Lager on board as the latest Major Partner with the new franchise preparing to make their debut in the 2028 NRL Season.

The three-year partnership further strengthens the brand’s long-standing connection to rugby league and communities across the country.

This will see SP Lager feature on the back of the PNG Chiefs’ playing shorts in the club’s inaugural NRL season in 2028 and in 2029, with additional support of the club in its pre-Foundation period throughout 2027.

As Major Partner, SP Lager will operate as the club’s exclusive alcoholic beverage provider and will hold exclusive pourage rights in corporate areas at PNG Chiefs home fixtures in PNG– subject to venue arrangements.

The partnership will also see the SP Lager logo feature prominently in stadium signage and media backdrop branding, while also providing hospitality, ticketing, and digital integration and match day activation opportunities.

SP Lager has a long-standing connection with rugby league in PNG including grassroots competitions, while its national reach will provide the opportunity to connect the PNG Chiefs with supporters across the country.

SP Lager and the PNG Chiefs will additionally work together on responsible drinking messaging and social outcomes as part of the framework, including key initiatives addressing domestic violence reduction across the country.

“SP Lager is a brand that has been part of PNG for generations and its connection with rugby league and communities across the country makes this a strong partnership for us,” PNG Chiefs CEO Lorna McPherson said.

“We know how important our commercial partners will be in helping us build a long-term sustainable club, and the reach, experience and genuine understanding of Papua New Guinea which the SP Lager brand has will be a huge asset to us.

“As a club, we also recognise that partnerships come with responsibility and we have worked closely with SP Lager to establish clear controls on how this agreement will work, particularly when it comes to young people and our community,” McPherson said.

“We’re looking forward to working together with SP Lager to create a strong and healthy partnership which benefits both organisations while ensuring that we continue to uphold the standards and values which the PNG Chiefs will stand for.”

SP Brewery Managing Director, Ed Weggemans said the partnership represents the continuation of SP Lager's long relationship with rugby league in Papua New Guinea.

“SP Lager's relationship with rugby league didn't begin with the PNG Chiefs – we have been part of this journey for generations,” he said. “From the SP Inter-City Cup in the 1990s, through our long-standing support of the SP PNG Hunters, and now alongside the PNG Chiefs, we have had the privilege of supporting the game as it has grown.

“The PNG Chiefs represent an extraordinary new chapter for PNG. For SP Lager, this is about continuing what we have always believed in – bringing Papua New Guineans together around the moments and passions we share.

“And importantly, we want Papua New Guineans to be part of this journey. “Through match day experiences, consumer activations and opportunities to get closer to the team, we want to bring the excitement of the PNG Chiefs to fans and communities across the country,” he added.

item.title: Gulf secures 80% of Papua LNG tier one benefit
item.description: After three months of negotiations, the multi-billion-kina Papua LNG Project has reached a significant milestone, with Gulf Province securing 80 percent of the Tier One benefits and Central Province receiving 20 percent. The verbal agreement was reached on Wednesday, following negotiations over the benefit-sharing arrangements between the two provinces.
item.content:encoded:
After three months of negotiations, the multi-billion-kina Papua LNG Project has reached a significant milestone, with Gulf Province securing 80 percent of the Tier One benefits and Central Province receiving 20 percent.

The verbal agreement was reached on Wednesday, following negotiations over the benefit-sharing arrangements between the two provinces.

Petroleum Minister Jimmy Maladina described the agreement as an important step towards establishing a fair, transparent and sustainable benefit-sharing framework for the Papua LNG Project.

Mr Maladina acknowledged the landowners and affected communities involved in the process, saying Tier One is a critical phase that establishes the foundation for the remaining negotiations and the eventual implementation of agreed benefits.

The agreement was signed at around 6pm by State representative and Petroleum Minister Jimmy Maladina, Oil and Gas Director David Manau and Acting Gulf Governor Morris Taudevin.

The signing was briefly paused following concerns raised by Central Governor Rufina Peter and other representatives from Gulf Province, who requested time to properly review the document before signing.

The signing later resumed, with the Central Governor, district representatives and LLG representatives proceeding with the agreement.

item.title: ICCC warns PMV and taxi operators against unapproved fare hikes
item.description: Public Motor Vehicle [PMV] and taxi operators in Port Moresby are planning to increase fares from Friday, but the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission [ICCC] says operators cannot increase fares without its approval. The planned fare increases come after fuel prices rose by K1 per litre, with operators citing higher fuel costs as the reason for the increase.
item.content:encoded:
Public Motor Vehicle [PMV] and taxi operators in Port Moresby are planning to increase fares from Friday, but the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission [ICCC] says operators cannot increase fares without its approval.

The planned fare increases come after fuel prices rose by K1 per litre, with operators citing higher fuel costs as the reason for the increase.

The ICCC says any increase in PMV and taxi fares resulting from higher fuel costs must first be assessed and approved by the Commission.

It says the current approved fares remain in place and operators should not impose higher fares without approval.

The ICCC has acknowledged the financial pressure faced by PMV and taxi operators in providing essential public transport services.

It says it is considering a practical way forward to address the impact of the recent fuel price increase on public transport.

The Commission is also due to make its annual adjustment to the maximum PMV and taxi fares for 2027 in about two months.

The ICCC says it will formally advise PMV and taxi operators as soon as a decision is made on how to address the current increase in fuel costs.

The latest fuel price increase is linked to volatility in the global fuel market, particularly the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

The ICCC says the Government is continuing to subsidise fuel prices to protect consumers from the full impact of higher international prices.

For example, diesel in Port Moresby is currently K5.90 per litre, compared with an estimated unsubsidised price of K7.31.

This represents a subsidy of K1.41 per litre, made up of a 66-toea GST exemption and a 75-toea direct subsidy paid to fuel importers.

The ICCC says higher fuel prices will put pressure on the cost of goods and services, particularly food, utilities, energy and transport.

However, it says the fuel price increase does not automatically authorise PMV and taxi operators to raise fares.

The Commission says it understands the challenges facing public transport operators and will fast-track a practical solution while continuing to protect consumers from unreasonable and excessive prices.

item.title: Family petitions over killing of Imbonggu man in Port Moresby
item.description: The Olgai/Welali tribesmen of Imbonggu District, Southern Highlands Province, have lodged a formal petition over the killing of 30-year-old father of three, Stanley Kera, in Port Moresby on September 14, 2026. The petition was received today by Assistant Commissioner of Police and NCD Central Commander Benjamin Turi.
item.content:encoded:
The Olgai/Welali tribesmen of Imbonggu District, Southern Highlands Province, have lodged a formal petition over the killing of 30-year-old father of three, Stanley Kera, in Port Moresby on September 14, 2026.

The petition was received today by Assistant Commissioner of Police and NCD Central Commander Benjamin Turi.

It is addressed to the Sugu Valley people of Kagua-Erave District, Southern Highlands, and the Purani people of Koroba-Kopiago District, Hela Province.

According to the petition, the killing followed a conflict on September 6 between the Purani people of South Koroba and the Sugu Valley people, in which a Purani man was killed.

The petition alleges that, in retaliation, Purani men mistakenly targeted and killed Kera, who was not involved in the earlier conflict.

Police confirmed the attackers were allegedly looking for people from Kagua, but Kera was from Imbonggu and was not involved in the dispute. No arrests have been made.

Tribal leader and former Kumul Telikom Holdings Limited Managing Director Jessie Wangua described Kera as “an innocent man caught between a fight involving two other groups.”

He said Kera had been in Port Moresby for only eight days and was preparing to travel to Australia under the Labour Mobility program.

“Stanley has left behind three children, a heavy burden now carried by his widow,” Mr Wangua said.

Mr Wangua stressed that compensation cannot replace criminal prosecution and said the family reserves its constitutional and legal rights, including pursuing remedies through the courts, Parliament and the media if the petition is ignored.

He said the petition calls on both groups to cooperate with law enforcement and honour custom to seek justice for Kera and prevent further loss of innocent life.

Meanwhile, Kera’s body is expected to arrive at his home in Walume Junction on friday.

item.title: US embassy champions digital future for PNG
item.description: The United States Chargé d’ Affaires to Papua New Guinea Alex M. Berenberg recently highlighted the US government’s expanding role in Papua New Guinea’s digital future. Two PNG digital leaders, Eugene Du Yerua and Lizarhmarie Warike, are currently in the United States under the International Visitor Leadership Program, engaging with experts on secure fiber optic networks.
item.content:encoded:
The United States Chargé d’ Affaires to Papua New Guinea Alex M. Berenberg recently highlighted the US government’s expanding role in Papua New Guinea’s digital future.

Two PNG digital leaders, Eugene Du Yerua and Lizarhmarie Warike, are currently in the United States under the International Visitor Leadership Program, engaging with experts on secure fiber optic networks.

Locally, the Embassy convened journalists, SMEs, and government officials for its “Digital Transformation at the Ground Level” forum, featuring innovators like University of Papua New Guinea student Belden Sakiromo, whose award winning “Bighet Rekod” system modernizes criminal records management.

“These efforts show the breadth of our partnership,” Berenberg said, “from digital transformation to defense, diplomacy, and commerce—anchored in shared values and building toward a resilient future.” Berenberg said.

Berenberg said PNG journalists recently joined a U.S. funded training on AI Technology in Journalism, equipping them with tools to navigate the opportunities and risks of emerging technologies.

He said these initiatives reflect a commitment to building capacity in PNG’s media and digital sectors, ensuring citizens can engage safely and securely in the digital era.

Beyond technology, the Embassy continues to strengthen ties through sports diplomacy, WWII history exchanges, and governance programs.

item.title: PNG Indonesia international land border to host small business trade fair
item.description: No man's land at Wutung International land border seperating Papua New Guinea and Indonesia will connect both nations through the Border Trade Fair, starting Thursday. The three days event is organized by Provincial Government of Papua in Indonesia and around 66 micro, small and medium enterprises from both nations will be setting up booths to talk commerce and find new business links.
item.content:encoded:
No man's land at Wutung International land border seperating Papua New Guinea and Indonesia will connect both nations through the Border Trade Fair, starting Thursday.

The three days event is organized by Provincial Government of Papua in Indonesia and around 66 micro, small and medium enterprises from both nations will be setting up booths to talk commerce and find new business links.

Papua New Guinea can take a page out of the success book of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises to the economy of its giant neighbour - Indonesia.

The MSMEs employs around 97 percent of the workforce in the fourth most populous country in the world.

The Border Trade Fair will run from October 8 to 10 between commonly referred to as "no men's land" the international land crossing from Wutung in West Sepik to Skouw in the Papua Province of Indonesia.

According to Jayapura Customs and Excise Office, export volume to PNG through the international land border is over K12 Million.

And the Border Trade Fair will be an opportunity for PNG Government to start moving the talks from Waigani to Vanimo to increase trade export to the massive economy of the country it shares the only land border with.

Papua Provincial Government of Indonesia and the Indonesian Embassy in a statement stated that, "The Border Trade Fair aims to strengthen corporation between the Republic of Indonesia and the Independent State of Papua New Guinea, particularly in the areas of cross-border trade, local economic development, investment, tourism, community empowerment, and people-to-people relations.

And further read "Indonesian entrepreneur can provide practical example of how to compose local products into attractive, competitive and marketable goods. At the same time, PNG SMEs can share their own traditional products, skills, and knowledge, creating a two-way exchange that can strengthen entrepreneurship and economic cooperation between Papua New Guinea and Indonesia."

item.title: Hailstorm batters food gardens in Enga
item.description: A heavy hailstorm has damaged food gardens and vegetation across four wards in Pilikambi LLG, Laiagam District, Enga Province.

item.title: 20 factory made guns surrendered in Koroba Lake Kopiago District
item.description: Four communities in Koroba–Lake Kopiago District, Hela Province, have voluntarily surrendered 20 factory-made firearms, more than 50 homemade guns, a hand grenade and various traditional weapons, including bows and arrows.
